# The bridge experiment

## The first trial

In the fictional town of Riverbend, engineer Anna tested a wooden footbridge in 2024.
The initial design used twelve beams and could carry 800 kilograms. During a rain test,
the untreated joints absorbed water and the deck shifted by three centimetres.
Anna stopped the trial before anyone crossed the bridge. This was a design failure,
not evidence that wooden bridges in general are unsafe.

## The revision

The team replaced the joints, added diagonal bracing and used a protective coating.
The revised design passed a static load test of 1,200 kilograms. A separate pedestrian
test involved six volunteers. The test did not establish performance during a flood.
The extra materials cost 240 fictional credits. Anna kept the twelve main beams.

## Lessons and limits

The example illustrates testing assumptions, preserving useful components and separating
measured results from expectations. The team measured displacement and load, not long-term
durability. A ten-year service life remains a target rather than an observed outcome.
The account contains no information about the bridge's carbon footprint.

This fixture is original synthetic test material written for brofessor. All people,
places, events and numerical results are fictional.
